# Project plan

## Start-up phase
<!--
Covering the planning phase, this section should provide a relatively
detailed plan of how work will start on the project. This section is
important because projects need to get up and running quickly.


 - [ ] Setting up collaboration platform inc. code for contributors etc.
 - [ ] License decisions
 - [ ] Reporting framework
-->

Nothing needs to be built to start. The public repository
<https://github.com/danielrak/genproc> already has an issue tracker,
R CMD check on Linux, macOS and Windows, code coverage, and automatic
deployment of the documentation site. In the first month a
`CONTRIBUTING.md`, a code of conduct and a "Milestone 1 review" GitHub
discussion are added and the coverage baseline is recorded. Reporting:
a monthly note to the ISC, a `NEWS.md` entry and a tagged release at
every milestone close.

## Technical delivery
<!--
Covering the actual delivery of the project this section should
provide at least a high-level description of the implementation.

Including target dates is really important as you need to be committed
and the ISC need to have a means of tracking delivery
-->

Dates assume a contract signed by December 2026 and work from January
2027.

**M1, by 2027-03-31. Contract.** The vignette and glossary described
above. Published for review; comments resolved before M2 code is
merged.

**M2, by 2027-05-31. `genproc_mask`.** S3 class with declared parameter
dependencies, input groups and a content-based `case_id`. Constructor,
validator, print method, tests for every documented mask pattern.
Release 0.3.0 tagged and submitted to CRAN.

**M3, by 2027-09-15. Execution layers.** `replay(result, case_id)`
re-runs one failed case from its recorded arguments and reports any
difference in inputs and package versions since the original run
(rebuilding past software environments is out of scope);
`method = "hash"` for content-hash input fingerprints; live progress of
non-blocking runs, collected in the background and queried on demand;
`cancel(job)` where the backend allows it, with a table of what each
backend supports. Release 0.4.0 tagged and submitted to CRAN.

**M4, by 2027-11-15. Evaluation and integration.** At least three users
outside the project run the documented tasks on 0.4.0: find a failed
case, read its traceback, re-run it, detect a changed input and re-run
the affected cases. What they could and could not do is published and
fixed where needed. A vignette shows a `genproc` run as one step of a
`targets` pipeline, with declared file dependencies and the pipeline's
behaviour when some cases fail.

**M5, by 2027-12-31. 1.0.0 and hand-over.** Lifecycle set to stable;
contributor guide, release checklist, design decisions and succession
process; a prospective co-maintainer recruited among reviewers and
evaluators and mentored through one release; closing post on the R
Consortium blog; software paper drafted for the R Journal.

## Other aspects

<!--
How will you ensure that your work is available to the widest number
of people? Please specify the open-source or creative commons license(s)

and how you will publicize your work. We encourage you to plan content

 - [ ] Announcement post

MIT code; CC BY 4.0 documentation, with the notice added in the first
month; public GitHub hosting during and after the grant. Communication:
announcement post at grant start, one R Consortium blog post per
quarter, delivery post at the end; a talk submitted to useR! 2027;
posts on Mastodon, Bluesky, LinkedIn and R-bloggers at each release.

## Budget & funding plan

<!--
Note that the maximum grant is $20k USD. The proposal should be in USD.

Outline the milestones for development and how much funding will be
required for each stage (as payments will be tied to project milestone
completion). This also helps the ISC in the event of partial funding.
Each milestone should specify the work to be done and the
expected outcomes, providing enough detail for the ISC to understand
the scope of the project work and assess the likelihood of success.

We expect that most of the budget will be allocated
for labor costs. We do not cover indirect costs. The ISC grants cannot
cover such things as travel, lodging, food, journal publication fees,
or personal hardware. Cloud services may be covered if they are specific
to the project and the project period. The ISC reserves the right to vet
how funds are used for each project separately. If in doubt, please reach
out to us.
-->

Total **13 000 USD**, labour only, 260 hours at 50 USD per hour; no
travel, hardware or cloud costs. The amounts allow partial funding in
the order listed, within the standard schedule of 50% at signature and
50% at completion.

| Milestone | Deliverable | Hours | USD |
|:----|:------------------------------------------------|----:|-------:|
| M1 | Contract vignette, glossary, retry rules, public review | 50 | 2 500 |
| M2 | `genproc_mask` class, compatibility suite, release 0.3.0 | 50 | 2 500 |
| M3 | Replay, hash fingerprints, live progress, cancel, release 0.4.0 | 80 | 4 000 |
| M4 | Evaluation by outside users, `targets` vignette | 40 | 2 000 |
| M5 | Release 1.0.0, governance, succession process, closing post | 40 | 2 000 |
